## Overview Reference implementation for RFC #63757, which covers the design, the alternatives and the interaction with #62749; design feedback is best placed there. This PR stays a draft for the RFC's feedback period. Model Runner V2 captures FULL decode graphs with `max_seq_len = max_model_len`. This PR adds, per context-length bound a module declares, a copy of each FULL decode graph captured with `max_seq_len = bound`, replayed only when every context in the step fits. GLM-5-Next's sparse indexer is the first user: within `index_topk` (2048 on GLM-5.3-Flash) its top-k is every causal token, so a decode step skips the indexer's q side and scoring. ## Claims - Model Runner V2, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` or `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: each FULL decode graph gets one copy per declared bound; a decode step replays it only when every request's context is within the bound, otherwise the default graph, as before. - GLM-5-Next (`Glm5NextForCausalLM`, `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`), kpool indexer without rope, CUDA and ROCm: a decode step whose contexts all fit `index_topk` skips `wq_b`, the head-weight projection, q quantization, paged-MQA logits and top-k in the FULL decode graphs captured for that bound. Eager steps and PIECEWISE graphs score as before. - GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4, MI355X, TP2, one image per request: - `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: output throughput +2.32 % (SE 0.44 pp) over concurrency 16-64, +4.6 % at concurrency 1, +12.3 % at 4. Text rows that cross or never fit 2048 tokens are within noise. GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run variation; sequential greedy outputs identical. - Breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: +4.50 % (SE 1.92 pp) over concurrency 16-64; greedy outputs identical. - Cost: one extra FULL decode graph per capture size and bound; on GLM-5.3-Flash TP2, CUDA graph memory 0.79 → 1.07 GiB per rank with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (12.55 → 12.82 GiB with breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) and KV cache −0.03 %. Opt-out: `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_specialize_seq_len": false}'`. - Unchanged: models that declare no bound; PIECEWISE, mixed FULL and micro-batched (DBO) graphs; prefill and mixed steps; PCP/DCP (feature off); Model Runner V1 graphs. ## Changes - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`: `BatchExecutionDescriptor.max_seq_len`, matched in `_is_compatible` like `max_query_len`; `_add_seq_len_bounded_graphs` adds the copies, captured after the default graphs and tried before them; `get_cudagraph_seq_len_bounds` collects the declared bounds below `max_model_len`. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, `dp_utils.py`: the step's bound, from the CPU arrays `prepare_inputs` uses for the metadata's `max_seq_len` (no device read), passed to dispatch per rank (not part of the DP sync). - `input_batch.py`, `model_states/default.py`, `model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`: a bounded graph's capture metadata has `max_seq_len = bound`. - `vllm/config/compilation.py`: `cudagraph_specialize_seq_len` (default on, like `cudagraph_specialize_lora`). - `vllm/models/glm5next/`: `Indexer` declares `index_topk` when the kpool op has its causal-fill path (`index_kpool > 1`, no indexer rope, CUDA-alike); `forward` computes the k side and gate score first, unchanged, then either calls the op with `q_quant=None, weights=None` or runs the q side. `_skips_scoring()` is True only while a FULL graph is being captured for a batch within the bound. Eager steps, including the warm-up run before each capture, score as before, so each warm-up compiles and autotunes everything its capture runs. The kpool ops accept the `None`s and assert q is present before scoring. - Second commit: the first commit also skipped scoring in eager decode steps within the bound, which made a cold start under breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` fail. The warm-up before the 1-token PIECEWISE capture took the skip path, so the scoring path's first call at that size came inside the capture. `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` specializes size 1, so `_fused_indexer_weight_scale` was recompiled there, and inductor's autotune synchronized inside the stream capture (`operation not permitted when stream is capturing`). A warm compile cache hid it. The second commit restricts the skip to FULL captures; the third adds its unit test. - Memory profiling counts the copies but estimates them low: on GLM-5.3-Flash TP2 the KV budget moved by 0.05 GiB while the copies took 0.28 GiB. ## Validation **Serving.** - Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-e4a5b5537344b103ed10de7764378ef09604ef3d` (vLLM `e4a5b55373`); its copies of every file this PR touches equal this PR's base. Baseline: the image as shipped; patched: the same with this PR's `vllm/` changes. - AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP2, `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` at revision `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`. - 3 launch pairs on the same 2 GPUs per pair, order alternating (baseline first, patched first, baseline first); The second commit changes only eager decode steps within the bound and the warm-up before each capture. Every decode step in these rows has at most 64 requests, and FULL decode graphs are captured up to 512 tokens, so these steps replay FULL graphs and do not reach the changed path. - Activation: every patched launch logs `Capturing 51 extra FULL decode CUDA graphs for context lengths <= (2048,).`; no baseline launch does. - Memory and startup: graph capture after KV cache allocation 1.07 GiB per rank patched vs 0.79 GiB baseline; KV cache 6,666,467 vs 6,668,288 tokens. The stall was not seen in 6 later patched c32 runs, 3 of them at the second commit. Cause not established. **Index equivalence.** For contexts 1-2048 at 1-512 rows, random and tied logits, and every decode top-k backend the indexer can select, the index rows the sparse MLA kernel reads after the scoring route equal those of the causal fill, element by element and in order.
